newsitem.title: UK: Airfreight industry can beat integrators - Unisys.
newsitem.headline: Airfreight industry can beat integrators - Unisys.

text.p: The traditional air cargo industry can outclass the performance of integrators as long as it aims for and achieves time-definite deliveries, a senior Unisys Corp executive said.

Hugh Doyle, Dublin-based managing director of the information management company's freight management transportation division, told a news briefing that shippers today demanded that their goods were delivered on time as promised.

He said that integrators -- companies such as DHL Worldwide Express and Federal Express Corp which attempt to tightly control all aspects of freight delivery -- achieved a reliability level of about 98 percent.
Doyle added that it took six days for the airline- and freight forwarder-driven "traditional" air cargo industry to move cargo from point of origin to destination -- just as it did 25 years ago.
"Although two percent of customers will always want tomorrow morning delivery, our investigations show that 95 percent of shippers require a 48-hour service," he noted.
"That is the way airfreight is moving," he said, adding that the "traditional" industry must recognise this trend and the demands of the marketplace.
He felt that if it did, then with the vast range of routes, aircraft and services it had at its disposal, the traditional air cargo industry could overcome the threat posed by integrators.
